name: hello
prompt:
Here is a Renyi program. It is run with the command-line arguments [] and no other input. Output exactly what the program prints to standard output, and nothing else: no explanation, no code fences.

module hello
  purpose: Greet whoever runs the program.

import std.console
import std.environment

public function main() needs console, environment
  purpose: Print a greeting that uses the first command-line argument as the name.

  let arguments be environment.arguments()
  let name be arguments.first() otherwise "world"
  console.print("Hello, {name}!")
end
